rows.canonicalDataStatus: Sheet identities, strict versioned documents, schema-v50 persistence, authoritative Trainer/Pokémon skill and reviewed equipment-provider modifiers, server-only journaled d6s, DC/opposed comparisons, atomic accepted results, and exact no-reroll operation replay are implemented. The GM-only workflow creates single, group, preset, explicit-DC, and opposed requests from exact sheets and controller ownership, observes pending responses, resolves ready checks, cancels with private reasons, and returns replay-safe receipts. The subject workflow projects only controlled Trainer/Pokémon prompts, canonical pools and visible modifiers, concealed-or-authorized DCs, aggregate readiness, legal accept/decline controls, own visible-or-withheld results, and durable server-owned timeout evidence. Structurally distinct GM, subject, and spectator projections provide full GM authority, own-subject safe history, and public labels, pending counts, generic history, and aggregate-or-withheld accepted outcomes respectively. All three rod flows require one accepted generic single-subject DC check bound to the exact actor, Skill, declaration, and one-use settlement; five embedded check/roll families intentionally retain their atomic or document-specific authority. Keyboard, touch, screen-reader, reduced-motion, desktop/mobile production liveplay, 320 CSS-pixel table-distance reflow, WCAG AA, no-leak, and bounded decision-surface performance acceptance are certified. Single/group reconnect, real SQLite restart, duplicate delivery, CAS concurrency, stale revision, two-boundary rollback, transient attention-publication failure, unresolved owner/GM campaign attention, and owner-safe terminal campaign history are certified; the generic Skill Check surface is native and complete.
rows.privacyImplications: Full notes, exact modifiers, controller and sheet bindings, journals, operations, diagnostics, and subject identities remain GM-only. Subjects receive only their own identity, skill authority, visible contributors, aggregate readiness, and own safe history/result. Spectators receive no prompt, subject, skill, DC, modifier, response identity, roll, total, journal, operation, private correction, or diagnostic authority. Campaign owner history exposes only a public label, terminal lifecycle, own outcome or explicit withholding, and time through an opaque entry identity; unresolved owner attention redacts the Profile identity.
